Sir,

At 7 p.m. 13/11/40 C.P.C. 2700 brought to the
station a pamphlet in Chinese which he stated he had
removed from the wall of Haining Road near North Honan
Road, subsequent to same having been posted by members

Notice of the Japanese Naval Landing Party
Settlement Section.
(1) Inhabitants should assist in arresting any
suspected male Chinese entering Japanese
controlled areas. They should prevent their
escape and report to the Japanese Naval
Landing Party or sentry in the vicinity.
(2) Those who do not comply with the above
instructions, or those who harbour suspects
will be seriously dealt with should same be
found out by the J.N.L.Party, and the area
concerned will be blockaded for an indefinite
period.
(3) Conditions having returned to normal in July
of this year J.N.L.Party removed the barriers
from North Kiangse Road. They have now been
closed again until such times as conditions
become peaceful again.
Dated 8/11/40.

日本海军陆战队

FFS 27 1:40

Barbed Wire Change
Hits Post Office

Parcel Business Decreases
Since Japanese Action

A difficult situation that will cripple the business of the Shanghai Post Office where Japanese censors are already working has been created as Japanese authorities have removed barbed wire entanglements, formerly placed near the Post Office blocking the Szechuen Road entrance, and have moved them to the end of the Kiangsi Road wooden bridge across the creek known to many as the "waterworks bridge." All those who send parcels to the Post Office must now pass through Japanese sentries on the Szechuen Road bridge.

Although the Japanese now do not require those who enter Hongkew to show passes they still enforce search regulations which fact causes a psychological restriction to be placed upon those who wish to send parcels to the Post Office. They must now pass through Japanese sentries while crossing the Szechuen Road bridge whereas three days ago they did not have to do that.

To save the trouble of having their parcels for outports (and therefore carefully sealed) examined by military authorities on the Szechuen Road bridge, many people have refrained from patronizing the Post Office since the barbed wire entanglements were moved. An official of the Post Office stated yesterday that the volume of business of the Parcel Department had decreased during the past few days.

It was also authoritatively learned that the matter had been referred to Settlement authorities for negotiations but so far no satisfactory results have been achieved. The Head Post Office in Kunming has been informed but it was said that Kunming could not do anything to remedy the situation here.

FFS 27 1:40

铁丝网变动
波及邮局

自日本采取行动以来
包裹业务减少

由于日本当局拆除了以前放置在邮局附近、阻塞四川路入口的铁丝网纠缠物，并将其移至许多人称为“水厂桥”的跨越小溪的江西路木桥尽头，造成了一种困难的局面，这将严重打击上海邮局的业务，而日本检查员已在该局工作。所有向邮局寄送包裹的人现在必须经过四川路桥上的日本哨兵。

虽然日本人现在不再要求进入虹口的人出示通行证，但他们仍然执行搜查规定，这一事实给希望向邮局寄送包裹的人造成了心理限制。他们现在穿越四川路桥时必须经过日本哨兵，而在三天前他们无需这样做。

为了避免在四川路桥上让军事当局检查寄往外埠的包裹（因此密封严密），许多人在铁丝网纠缠物被移动后便不再光顾邮局。邮局的一位官员昨天表示，过去几天包裹部的业务量有所下降。

另据权威消息获悉，此事已提交租界当局进行谈判，但迄今未取得满意结果。昆明总局已获知此事，但据说昆明方面无法采取任何措施来改善这里的状况。

3/78/2.

CONFERENCE HELD AT BRITISH MILITARY HEADQUARTERS 11.9.39.

The Conference assembled at British Military
Headquarters, Tifeng Road Camp at 1400 hours 11 September,
1939.

Present :- Commander Kurihara, Japanese Naval
Landing Party.
Mr. Tsujino.
Major B.H. Ashmore, Brigade Major.
Major S.R. Hunt, Liaison Officer.

Subject :- To discuss proposals relating to the
return to the Japanese Naval Landing
Party control of the area in "B" Sector
bounded by RANGE ROAD on the North,
N. KIANGSU ROAD on the East, SOOCHOW
CREEK on the South and N. HONAN ROAD
on the West.

（印：OFFICIAL SEAL）

Major Ashmore stated it was understood that the Japanese
Naval Landing Party wished to move up to the original
boundary which existed between "A" and "B" Sectors before
the 1937 hostilities. Namely to the line of NORTH HONAN ROAD
which is inclusive to the British Sector. Where did the
Japanese Naval Landing Party propose to place their boundary,
wire or barricades ?

Commander Kurihara stated that they were prepared to make the
following proposals :-

(i) That the line of barriers should remain as
at present on NORTH KIANGSU ROAD.
(ii) That notice boards in English, Japanese and
Chinese should be erected at entrances to main
roads to the East of NORTH HONAN ROAD stating
this was Japanese Defence Sector.
(iii) That the Japanese Naval Landing Party and
the Shanghai Municipal Police should be
responsible for the maintenance of law and order
in this area. S.M.P. should continue functioning
as at present.
(iv) Naval Landing Party patrols operating daily
up to line of NORTH HONAN ROAD exclusive.
(v) The inhabitants of the area will NOT require
passes and there will be NO restrictions imposed.
In fact everything should remain as at present in
this respect.
(vi) That special protection should be afforded if
required to any British subjects residing in the
area and that Redemption Building will be regarded
as most important.

Major Ashmore
pages.zh:
3/78/2.

1939年9月11日在英国军事总部举行的会议。

会议于1939年9月11日14时在提丰路（Tifeng Road）营地的英国军事总部召开。

出席人员：日本海军陆战队栗原（Kurihara）指挥官。
辻野（Tsujino）先生。
B.H. 阿什莫尔（Ashmore）少校，旅参谋长。
S.R. 亨特（Hunt）少校，联络官。

议题：讨论关于将“B”区内由兰路（北）、江苏路（东）（N. KIANGSU ROAD）、苏州河（南）和河南路（西）所包围的区域交还日本海军陆战队控制的提议。

（印：官方印章）

阿什莫尔少校表示，据理解，日本海军陆战队希望推进至1937年战事发生前“A”区和“B”区之间原有的边界线。即推进至包括在英国区范围内的河南路（北段）一线。日本海军陆战队提议将其边界、铁丝网或路障设置在哪里？

栗原指挥官表示，他们准备提出以下建议：

(i) 路障线应保持在目前江苏路（北段）的位置。
(ii) 应在河南路（北段）以东的主要道路入口处设立用英文、日文和中文书写的告示牌，声明此为日本防御区。
(iii) 日本海军陆战队和上海公共租界工部局警务处应共同负责维持该区域的治安。工部局警务处应继续按现状运作。
(iv) 海军陆战队巡逻队每日行动至河南路（北段）一线（不含该路）。
(v) 该区域居民不需要通行证，也不会施加任何限制。事实上，在这方面一切应保持现状。
(vi) 如有需要，应为居住在该区域的任何英国臣民提供特别保护，且救火会大楼（Redemption Building）将被视为最重要设施。

阿什莫尔少校

pages.en:
- 2 -

Major Ashmore stated these proposals were much appreciated and would receive immediate consideration. The following proposals were made :-

(i) That no action will be taken in respect of this change until notification has been made to the inhabitants by the S.M.P. and in any case no action before the 21st September, 1939.

(ii) That both parties will issue very strict instructions to their troops respecting the boundary line in order that trouble may be avoided.

(iii) That the British posts at "A" Blockhouse and the Telephone Exchange be withdrawn on the agreed date for the new arrangement to become operative.

(iv) That persons would have full access to PURDON MARKET.

(v) The notification to the Public that the area will come under Japanese control shall be made by the S.M.P. as soon as possible after this agreement is signed by both parties.

(vi) The notification to the Public shall contain statements to the effect that :-

(a) The change in control will not be effected before 21st September, 1939.

(b) That this change is regarded as a step towards the restoration of the conditions existing in the area prior to 1937 hostilities.

(c) That no passes will be required and that no restrictions will be imposed.

(d) That J.M.L.P. patrols may be seen operating daily in the area.

(e) That the S.M.P. will continue to exercise police control.

All the proposals made by the Japanese and British were tentatively agreed upon pending their submission for consideration to the Commandant Ashmore.

Commander Furukawa asked that consideration might be given to the opening of the barrier at "B" Blockhouse (NORTH ROHAN ROAD) in order to facilitate movement to the North Station area.

Major Ashmore pointed out that NORTH ROHAN ROAD was at present very congested and additional traffic would not improve the situation.

Commander Furukawa replied that it would be their plan to institute a post in the vicinity of NORTH ROHAN ROAD - BOUNDARY ROAD junction where passes would be checked and traffic would at first be limited to pedestrians only.

/Major Ash.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

阿什莫尔（Ashmore）少校表示，这些提议备受赞赏，并将得到立即审议。提出的提议如下：-

(i) 在工部局警务处（S.M.P.）向居民发出通知之前，不会就此次变更采取任何行动，且无论如何，在1939年9月21日之前不采取任何行动。

(ii) 双方将向其部队发布关于边界线的非常严格的指令，以避免发生麻烦。

(iii) “A”号碉堡和电话交换局的英国哨所将在商定日期撤出，以便新安排生效。

(iv) 人员将拥有进入普顿市场（PURDON MARKET）的完全通道。

(v) 在双方签署本协议后，工部局警务处应尽快向公众发出该区域将置于日本控制之下的通知。

(vi) 向公众发出的通知应包含如下内容的声明：-

(a) 控制权的变更不会在1939年9月21日之前实施。

(b) 此次变更被视为恢复1937年战事之前该区域既存状况的一步。

(c) 不需要通行证，也不会施加任何限制。

(d) 可以看到日本海军陆战队（J.M.L.P.）巡逻队每天在该区域活动。

(e) 工部局警务处将继续行使警察管制权。

日本和英国提出的所有提议均获暂定同意，待提交给指挥官阿什莫尔（Commandant Ashmore）审议。

古川（Furukawa）中校请求考虑开放“B”号碉堡（北罗汉路，NORTH ROHAN ROAD）的路障，以方便前往北站区域。

阿什莫尔少校指出，北罗汉路目前非常拥堵，增加交通流量并不会改善局势。

古川中校回答说，他们的计划是在北罗汉路与界路（BOUNDARY ROAD）交界处附近设立一个哨所，在那里检查通行证，且起初交通仅限于行人。

/阿什少校（Major Ash.

pages.en:
- 3 -

Major Ashmore stated the matter would be placed before the
General and receive consideration. The Japanese would be
notified of the result of this consideration. It was agreed

Ta Mei Chou Pao (Weekly Edition of Ta Mei Pao), Hwa Pao,
Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao, Chinese-American Daily News:

JAPANESE SOLDIERS ENCIRCLING NORTH SZECHUEN ROAD TO
CONDUCT A STRICT SEARCH

At about 9 a.m. yesterday, a body of some 500
Japanese gendarmes encircled North Szechuen Road, Tsepoo
Road, Tiendong Road and Wuchang Road to conduct a strict
search. Pedestrians were prohibited free movement on the
roadway and traffic at the Garden Bridge and the
Szechuen Road Bridge was interrupted for 15 minutes. The
situation was very tense in the area under search. The
Japanese gendarmes made a house-to-house search, questioning
pedestrians very strictly, and many suspicious-looking
persons were arrested. The search lasted for about one
hour and normalcy was restored.
It is learned that the cause of this search is
because the Japanese were informed that a large anti-
Japanese gang was reported to be active in the area north
of the Soochow Creek.

**JAPANESE SOLDIERS SEARCH HUNG AN LI ON RANGE ROAD**

Under the leadership of two officers, 11 armed Japanese soldiers on the night of September 26,27 went to Hung An Li (鴻安里) on Range Road (between North Honan Road and North Kiangse Road) and conducted a house-to-house search of the alleyway. CONDITIONS IN "A" SECTOR

Since the Japanese took over "A" Sector, the
people living in that area have become uneasy.
The Japanese soldiers have established an anti-
cholera injection depot to the right of the Shanghai
Telephone Company at the corner of North Kiangse Road and
Haining Road and residents in the sector have been forced
to attend at the depot for anti-cholera injections. The
period of injection has been extended from September 30
to October 10.
Owing to overcrowding at the injection depot,
many cases of people being beaten by City Government
policemen with batons have occurred. The Shanghai
Municipal Police have posted several Chinese, one Sikh and
one Japanese policemen near the depot and have marked out
a passage with barbed wire barricades.
Japanese soldiers are patrolling the various
alleyways and residents have been notified that, commencing
from to-morrow, all residents must report the number of
people staying in their houses and must produce their
anti-cholera injection certificates before they are allowed
to reside in the area. Certificates must be posted on
the doors of their houses.
Upon learning of this, the residents became
anxious. Yesterday afternoon our reporter made an
inspection of that area and noticed many people removing
from North Honan Road and North Kiangse Road.
Recently a number of City Government policemen
in the Temple of the Queen of Heaven on North Honan Road were
driven off by British patrols. Yesterday more than ten
City Government policemen were seen in the Temple standing by
unarmed at the Pass Issuing Depot; they were interrogating
persons who had called to apply for passes. Formerly
persons applying for a pass had to pay in notes of the Hwa
Shing Bank, but now legal tender notes are accepted.
British sentries were still on duty at the
corner of North Honan Road and Range Road as well as at the
corner of North Honan Road and Haining Road. Barbed wire
barricades on Boundary Road were still there as were those
installed by the Japanese soldiers from Kiangse Road Bridge
to Range Road. Japanese sentries are still on duty at
the corner of North Kiangse Road and Boone Road and at the
corner of North Kiangse Road and Haining Road. Pedestrians
have to show their passes for examination at these passages.

“A”区局势

自日军接管“A”区以来，居住在该地区的民众变得不安。日军在江西路北路与海宁路拐角处的上海电话公司右侧设立了一个霍乱防疫注射站，该区居民被强制前往该站接受霍乱防疫注射。注射期已从9月30日延长至10月10日。
由于注射站拥挤不堪，发生多起市政府警察用警棍殴打民众的事件。上海公共租界工部局警务处已在注射站附近部署数名华捕、一名锡克捕和一名日捕，并用铁丝网路障划定了一条通道。
日军士兵正在各条弄堂巡逻，并已通知居民，从明天起，所有居民必须申报家中居住人数，并出示霍乱防疫注射证书，方可获准在该区域居住。证书必须张贴在自家门上。
得知此消息后，居民们感到焦虑。昨天下午，本报记者对该地区进行了视察，注意到许多人正从河南北路和江西路北路搬离。
最近，河南北路天后庙内的一些市政府警察被英国巡逻队驱赶。昨天，在天后庙的发证处，可以看到十多名市政府警察手无寸铁地站立着；他们正在盘问前来申请通行证的人。以前，申请通行证者必须支付华兴银行的钞票，但现在接受法定货币钞票。
英国哨兵仍在河南北路与兰路（Range Road）的拐角处，以及河南北路与海宁路的拐角处执勤。界路（Boundary Road）上的铁丝网路障依然存在，日军士兵从江西路桥到兰路安装的路障也依然存在。日本哨兵仍在江西路北路与百老汇路（Boone Road）的拐角处，以及江西路北路与海宁路的拐角处执勤。行人必须在这些通道出示通行证以供检查。

Subject Re Report of Japanese Military functioning at the junction of

Made by A.S. Devon Forwarded by Officer i/c. Director:

Sir,
At 3 p.m. 24-7-39, P.C. Chu Meng reported to the
station that whilst making enquiries on North Kiangse Road near
Ligin Road he had observed the Japanese Military carry out
accessory operations at the junction of these roads.
The undersigned, accompanied by D.P.D. Turnbull (Hongkew)
visited the scene, where it was observed that four marines and
an officer of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, had stationed
themselves in an opening in the barbed-wire and were busily
engaged in examining passes of persons entering and leaving
that area (east of North Kiangse Road), refusing passage to
those not in possession of a pass.
The Officer, Lieut. Nomimoto, was interviewed and offered
the following explanation for their actions.
"Due to the congestion of the residents in that area it
has been found necessary to take precautionary measures to
combat an outbreak of cholera. A marquee has been set up
on Mining Road, east of North Kiangse Road, where residents
of the area must obtain cholera inoculations and registration
certificates. For the present, until a satisfactory standard
has been reached, inspection parties will operate at irregular
periods to instruct the residents of the absolute necessity
of obtaining inoculation against cholera."
The period of inspection today was from 3 p.m. until
3.45 p.m. after which time the party withdrew and permitted
free passage to one and sundry.
Nothing untoward happened at the scene of inspection.

Sgt. Det. i/c. D.D.O.'C' Div. W. Sevan

ir,
Reference previous reports in connection with this case
detectives posted at the sub-divisional office report changes now,
relative to the effect that 4 sub-tenants and families removed
during the clearance ending 6 p.m. 21-7-39. These evacuees, it
was learned, intend taking up residence with their friends and
relatives in districts south of the zone's area.
No moves are reported from any other part of the area
in question.
Several of the chief-tenants removed boxes and trunks for
safe keeping in the homes of friends, but they themselves did
not remove.
From enquiries made among the evacuees the following
reasons are given for their unwillingness to reside in the
area in question.
1. Objection to inoculation.
2. Cost of pass.
3. Inconvenience to south of the Creek workers returning
to their homes via Japanese Controlled bridges.
4. Objection to residing in Japanese Controlled territory.
Attempts were made to erect shelters on North Fiangse Road
but this was prevented and persons dispersed by Inspector Gash,
Officer i/c. and party.
Japanese Military patrols were seen to be active in
alleyways bordering North Fiangse Road as well as on Boone
Road.
Seaford Highlanders Officer attended and posted a
patrol.

At 6.20 p.m. June 28, 1939, C.P.C. 1656, attached
to West Hongkew, telephoned the station and reported
that Japanese soldiers were removing barbed wire in
the vicinity of Boone Road east of North Kiungse Road.

S. I. Brown and the undersigned immediately visited
the scene where it was observed that some twenty to
thirty members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party were
engaged in erecting barbed wire on the north and south
sides of Boone Road, between North Kiungse Road and North
Szechuen Road (no man's land), not removing wire as
reported by the aforementioned constable.

Enquiries were made among residents in the vicinity,
but no one could proffer any explanation for the sudden
action on the part of the Japanese Authorities.

action is similar to that reported by Inspector Cash,
Officer i/c, on June 20, 1939.

先生，

1938年7月4日下午2时，居住在愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）、电话号 80190 的 Lo Zau Ban（曹幼班）先生与其看守梁春旺（Liang Tsung Ong，华人）一同来到警署，报告称在1938年7月3日凌晨2时30分左右，海宁路468弄9号和11号（其 former residence）车库的部分墙体被不明人士破坏。噪音惊醒了看守，他前去查看但未看到任何人。显然，此人/这些人听到看守走近便逃走了。

1938年7月3日下午4时30分左右，一名身穿西式服装、体型较胖、身高约5英尺9英寸的日本男子，从海宁路沿弄堂走到该房屋并敲前门。他做出想进屋看看的手势，看守允许其进入。双方通过书写汉字进行交流。

该日本男子查看了两栋房屋的所有房间，并表示想“借用”一些家具和字画。看守称他无法做主，需征得主人同意。该男子在屋内停留约十至十五分钟后离开。

大约又过了十五分钟，该男子与一名身穿和服的日本女子一同返回，两人一起查看了各个房间。

离开房屋时，该男子表示他们将于1938年7月4日下午2时左右回来，以了解是否可以借用部分家具。他留下一张纸条，上面用英文和日文写着 P. Suemitsu 先生。

Subject: Erection of barbed wire _________________ I.J.P.
Made by. ____ Miller. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

At 1.45 p.m. to-day a message was received at the station
that members of the J.N.L.P. were erecting barbed wire
barricades across Route 201 and other streets leading from
Kiangse Road thus preventing entry or exit of the Chinese
population in that sector.

Inspector Chapman immediately proceeded to the scene attended.
The "C" Division was also notified and attended.

With the closure of all roads leading to and from knife
rests across Route 201 and other streets it was impossible for
any person to pass along Kiangse Road nor was it possible
for any vehicle to pass in either direction.

The reason given for this action by the J.N.L.P.
was that they had been ordered by their authorities to allow the Chinese
to remain in the sector themselves.

先生，

今天下午1时45分，警署收到消息，称日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.P.）成员正在江西路（Kiangse Road）及其他街道上架设铁丝网路障，从而阻止该区域中国居民的进出。

Chapman 督察立即前往现场处理。“C”区也接到通知并派人到场。

Japanese Barrier - 8-5-38.
Made by ____ Elders Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 2.30 p.m. on the 8-5-38 Mr. C. Liang, Chinese,
residing at No. 9, Lane 468 Gate Victor Emanuel Rd., came
to the Station and reported that the Japanese had moved their
barrier on Haining Road from its original position near North
Szechuen Road to a point further west towards North Kiangse Road
and this had resulted in his Chinese caretaker who was looking
after certain houses on Haining Road, being enclosed within the
barrier. Mr. Liang requested the Police to ascertain whether
his caretaker was still there.

[Stamp: SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 10 MAY 1938]

Mr. Suda visited the scene and con-
ducted enquiries.

It was ascertained that during the morning of the 8-5-38
the Japanese Naval Authorities had moved their barrier on
Haining Road from its original position near North Szechuen
Road further west to a point about 50 yards east of North
Kiangse Road and have strengthened it and made it impassable.
The reason for this being the better protection of the Japanese
concession on duty in that area.

Mr. Liang is the owner of Houses Nos. 470, 472 and 474
Haining Road and House 3 Lane 468 Haining Road. These houses
are located on the Japanese side of the barrier. The caretaker
is residing in House No. 3 together with another Chinese man
and his wife and child who are Mr. Liang's tenants. The other
houses are unoccupied. The gates of the lane are locked and the
caretaker keeps the keys. The lane is a cul-de-sac. The
Naval Authorities state they do not mind those Chinese residing
there for the present provided there is no trouble but insist
on the lane gates being kept locked.

先生，

1938年5月8日下午2时30分，居住在意帝亚路（Victor Emanuel Rd.）9号的华人 C. Liang 先生来到警署，报告称日本人已将海宁路的路障从原靠近北四川路的位置向西移至更靠近北江西路（North Kiangse Road）的一点，导致其负责看管海宁路某些房屋的华人看守被围在路障内。Liang 先生请求警方查明其看守是否仍在那里。

[印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1938年5月10日]

Suda 先生前往现场并
进行了查询。

经查实，1938年5月8日上午，日本海军当局将海宁路的路障从原靠近北四川路的位置向西移至北江西路以东约50码处，并加强了路障，使其无法通行。此举旨在更好地保护在该区域执勤的日本租界利益。

Liang 先生是海宁路470、472和474号房屋以及海宁路468弄3号房屋的所有者。这些房屋位于路障的日方一侧。看守与另一名华人男子及其妻儿（均为 Liang 先生的租户）居住在3号房屋内。其他房屋无人居住。弄堂大门紧锁，钥匙由看守保管。该弄堂为死胡同。海军当局表示，只要不惹麻烦，他们目前不介意那些华人住在那里，但坚持要求弄堂大门保持上锁状态。
